doc.title: Artie Shaw — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Own bands: swing concert, Brunswick, RCA
title: The Deserted Farm and MacDowell's estate; respect for classical composers
summary: The MacDowell transcription was withheld because of the estate, while Shaw says he respected composers more than Tommy Dorsey did with Rachmaninoff.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Did he do The Deserted Farm [sic: A Deserted Farm] as well?
No. That was done by . . . I don’t remember who wrote that. But that was a direct transcription of the piano music.

Oh yeah. Not a note changed. Except where [Shaw sings a five-note melodic phrase] I played it [Shaw sings the same phrase, but with a jazz swing rhythm]. Give it a groove. Mistakes stopped it. They didn’t want it.
They didn’t release it at the time.
I didn’t want to fight with Mrs. MacDowell.
They didn’t like the idea of it treated as a popular record, because it had a rhythm section. He wrote it free form.
Just for the record, we better say who wrote the song. This is The Deserted . . .

He was one of the American composers. Oddly enough. It was strange, because I had a lot of respect for that stuff. I didn’t want to bowdlerize it, and yet here comes Tommy Dorsey with Once Upon A Midnight and The Moon And My . . . what? . . . [Shaw sings a melodic phrase] . . . beautiful Rachmaninoff. They never consulted Rach . . . Everybody knew those pieces. I wouldn’t have dreamt of doing that, like taking Ravel’s La Valse and making a jazz piece out of it. Terrible. You could do it. The notes were there. But I thought, gee, you’ve got to have some respect for these guys. When I did Deserted Farm, oddly enough that was the only one that stayed with the original piece,
and that was not released. Whereas the others, which were total bowdlerizations of the intent of the composers, went out and became hits. Strange anomaly. We’re back to the public. What they’ll buy.
